 Cyclone Akvan: IMD warns of extremely heavy rainfall, 145 kmph winds along Andhra coast

 Edited by Mahima Sharma / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Nov 17, 2026, 13:41 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium
 Large
 Print Cyclonic Storm Akvan is brewing over the Bay of Bengal and is set to escalate rapidly. (Pic Credit: Agency) Cyclonic Storm Akvan, currently positioned over the central parts of the south and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal, is expected to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm by the morning of November 19 before making landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast around noon on November 20, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said on Tuesday. According to the IMD's national bulletin issued at 2:30 am IST on November 17, the storm remained nearly stationary over the previous nine hours and continued to be centred over the same region. Watch Cyclone Arnab Strikes Andhra, Odisha: Seawater Floods Homes, Trees Uprooted, Trains & Flights Hit The weather system was located near latitude 12.2°N and longitude 85.7°E, around 610 km east of Chennai in Tamil Nadu, 630 km northeast of Trincomalee in Sri Lanka, 660 km southeast of Machilipatnam in Andhra Pradesh, 670 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam and 790 km south of Gopalpur in Odisha, according to the news agency ANI. The IMD said the storm is likely to move north-northwestwards and strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal by the evening of November 17. It is subsequently expected to continue moving northwestwards and intensify further into a very severe cyclonic storm by the morning of November 19. According to the forecast, the system will continue its northwestward movement before crossing the Andhra Pradesh and yanam coasts between Nellore and Tuni around noon on November 20. At the time of landfall, the cyclone is expected to generate maximum sustained wind speeds of 120-130 kmph, with gusts reaching up to 145 kmph, the bulletin stated. The IMD has issued an orange alert for the Andhra Pradesh coast and adjoining coastal areas of south Odisha, warning of the potential impact of the approaching cyclone. Heavy rainfall warning for Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh
 The weather department has forecast light to moderate rainfall at several places across north Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal on November 17 and 20, with isolated areas likely to receive heavy rainfall. Heavy to very heavy rainfall is also expected at isolated places on November 18 and 19, potentially causing waterlogging in parts of Tamil Nadu. For coastal Andhra Pradesh, the IMD has predicted light to moderate rainfall at several locations, accompanied by heavy showers at isolated places on November 18. Join conversation

 The situation could intensify on November 19 and 20, with isolated areas of north coastal Andhra Pradesh likely to receive extremely heavy rainfall exceeding 21 cm. Odisha also likely to receive heavy rainfall
 In Odisha, isolated areas are likely to experience heavy rainfall on November 18, with light to moderate showers expected at some places. The IMD has further forecast light to moderate rainfall across most places in the state, along with heavy to very heavy showers at isolated locations between November 19 and 21. The weather department's latest warning indicates that the approaching cyclone could bring intense rainfall and strong winds to several coastal districts, particularly in Andhra Pradesh and adjoining regions.
